summary: US forces conducted a 12th consecutive night of strikes against Iranian military targets, including naval capabilities, missile storage, and air defense assets. Iran launched ballistic missiles at Aqaba, Jordan, with explosions heard in Eilat, Israel. President Trump declared a new policy: any Iranian fire toward vessels in the Strait of Hormuz will trigger US strikes on Iranian bridges or power plants, including near Tehran.
key_points: US CENTCOM completed 12th consecutive night of strikes on Iranian military targets including naval capabilities, missile storage, and air defense systems. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/380069)
Iran fired 4 missiles toward western Jordan, targeting Aqaba; explosions heard in Israel's southern city of Eilat. (Source: @manniefabian/58824)
Trump announced US will bomb one Iranian bridge or power plant per Iranian attack on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, including targets near Tehran. (Source: @lelotsenzura/93813)
US missile attack on Shalamcheh border crossing between Iran and Iraq killed two pilgrims, per Khuzestan officials. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/380055)
Multiple explosions reported in Bushehr, Iran, near air base, possibly from US strikes launched from Bahrain. (Source: @kianmeli1/89943)
IRGC Aerospace Commander threatened to cut electricity to Gulf states if US attacks Iranian bridges or power plants. (Source: @asafroz/51787)
CENTCOM naval blockade in Arabian Sea redirected 9 commercial vessels and disabled 1 as of July 22. (Source: @shin_persian/8379)
UK evacuating personnel from Iran due to escalating situation. (Source: @New_security8200/202857)

sections.executive_summary: US forces conducted a 12th consecutive night of strikes against Iranian military targets, including naval capabilities, missile storage, and air defense assets. Iran launched ballistic missiles at Aqaba, Jordan, with explosions heard in Eilat, Israel. President Trump declared a new policy: any Iranian fire toward vessels in the Strait of Hormuz will trigger US strikes on Iranian bridges or power plants, including near Tehran.

points: US CENTCOM conducted 12th consecutive night of strikes targeting Iranian naval capabilities, missile and drone storage facilities, coastal surveillance sites, and air defense assets, degrading Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/380069)

Multiple explosions reported in Bushehr at 00:49 local time, including two consecutive powerful blasts near the air base and Behmani area, with witnesses confirming the city was hit; strikes reportedly supported by US missile launches from Bahrain. (Source: @kianmeli1/89943)

Explosions heard in Ahvaz at 00:10 Thursday morning; additional blasts reported in Bandar Mahshahr and Islamabad-e Gharb in Kermanshah province, per local sources. (Source: @kianmeli1/89935, @Faytuks_Network/5573, @VahidOnline/77416)

IRGC Aerospace Force Commander Brig. Gen. Seyyed Majid Moosavi warned that attacks on Iranian bridges and power plants would guarantee power outages for US allies in the Gulf. (Source: @presstv/199962)
Tehran judiciary reiterated ban on import, sale, and use of satellite internet equipment including Starlink, with penalties for violations. (Source: @kianmeli1/89941)
IRIB broadcast subtitle instructing citizens to shoot at any enemy aircraft or helicopter spotted. (Source: @kianmeli1/89934)
High alert across Israeli air defense arrays for potential Iranian attack following missile launches toward Jordan. (Source: @yediotnews25/133059)
Explosions heard in Eilat, Israel's southernmost city, amid Iranian ballistic missile attack on neighboring Jordanian city of Aqaba. (Source: @manniefabian/58824)

IDF revealed 12 Palestinian footballers, coaches, and a FIFA referee were actually Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad operatives, including several who participated in October 7 attacks; list includes battalion commanders, company commanders, and anti-tank unit members. (Source: @amitsegal/63271)
Government told Supreme Court it could not complete legislation for October 7 inquiry committee due to scheduling constraints, will resume after elections. (Source: @amitsegal/63267)

IDF exposed 12 Gazan footballers, coaches, and a FIFA international referee as Hamas and PIJ militants, some involved in October 7 infiltration; includes deputy battalion commander of Nuseirat, air wing company commander, and anti-tank operatives. (Source: @amitsegal/63271)
Hamas official Khalil al-Hayya called for Palestinian unity, rejected displacement of residents, and urged strengthening regional ties amid US-Iran war. (Source: @N12chat/218713)
Enemy aircraft dropped flares over the town of Zoutar al-Sharqiya in southern Lebanon. (Source: @redlinkleb/32566)
Artillery shelling reported on Nabatieh al-Fawqa in southern Lebanon. (Source: @redlinkleb/32570)

US missile attack on Shalamcheh border crossing passenger terminal between Iran and Iraq killed two pilgrims as preliminary toll; Khuzestan security deputy confirmed strike by 'American terrorist enemy'. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/380055)
Shargh Daily reported missile attack around Shalamcheh border terminal; Khuzestan official stated no casualties and pilgrim traffic unaffected. (Source: @SharghDaily/173895)
Initial reports of US airdrop near Anbar province approaches in western Iraq. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/380067)
Explosions reported in Erbil, capital of Iraq's Kurdistan Region. (Source: @yediotnews25/133064)
IRGC Aerospace Commander threatened to cut electricity to Gulf states if US attacks Iranian bridges or power plants. (Source: @asafroz/51787)
CENTCOM naval blockade in Arabian Sea redirected 9 commercial vessels and disabled 1 as of July 22; USS Michael Murphy (DDG 112) monitoring operations. (Source: @shin_persian/8379)
UKMTO reported tanker struck by unknown projectile 70NM southwest of Al Shuqaiq, Saudi Arabia, causing onboard fire; crew fighting fire, no casualties reported. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/5576)
Trump declared new policy: any Iranian fire at vessels in Strait of Hormuz will trigger US bombing of one Iranian bridge or power plant, including near Tehran. (Source: @lelotsenzura/93813)
US announced signing of nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia. (Source: @amitsegal/63277)

Secretary of State Rubio stated Iran violated nuclear understanding by attacking a ship the day it was to issue a statement; understanding included reopening Hormuz and guaranteeing free navigation; China opposes Iran's Hormuz actions and tolls. (Source: @VahidOnline/77410)

sections.threat_assessment: The conflict has entered a dangerous phase of direct kinetic exchange: US strikes on Iranian territory for 12 consecutive nights, Iranian ballistic missile retaliation against a US partner (Jordan), and explicit US threats to strike Iranian critical infrastructure including near Tehran. Iran's threat to target Gulf energy infrastructure creates a regional escalation ladder. The naval blockade and tanker attack indicate expanding maritime conflict. Israel remains on high alert for spillover. The killing of pilgrims at a border crossing adds a sectarian dimension that could mobilize Shiite militias in Iraq.
sections.regional_response: Jordan absorbed an Iranian missile strike on Aqaba without public retaliation. Gulf states face explicit Iranian threats to their power grids. Saudi Arabia signed a nuclear agreement with the US amid the crisis. China criticized Iran's Hormuz actions. The UK evacuated personnel from Iran. Iraq hosts US airdrops near Anbar and suffers spillover explosions in Erbil. Lebanon experiences Israeli flare drops and shelling. Palestinian factions call for unity amid the broader war.
sections.intelligence_notes: The 12-night US strike campaign suggests a systematic degradation of Iranian air defense and missile capabilities. Bushehr explosions near a nuclear facility raise concerns about targeting thresholds. Trump's Hormuz policy creates a clear red line with automatic retaliation. The Shalamcheh border strike indicates US willingness to hit IRGC logistics nodes. The naval blockade enforcement shows expanded maritime interdiction. IDF's exposure of footballer-operatives reveals continued Hamas military integration into civilian structures. Iran's domestic internet restrictions suggest preparation for information control during conflict.
